study type: Retrospective cohort study (population-based analysis of birth records)
exposure: interaction between underweight status and race/ethnicity
interaction between underweight status and public insurance
cohort: The study included 3,070,241 singleton births with linked hospital discharge records from California between 2011 and 2017.
finding: Being underweight preconception is associated with an increased risk of preterm birth (PTB) and small for gestational age (SGA), with these effects varying by race/ethnicity and insurance status.
birth_weight: Small for gestational age (SGA) was an outcome, which is defined based on birth weight.
gest_age: Preterm birth (PTB) and small for gestational age (SGA) were outcomes, both of which are defined using gestational age.
